mainEntity.name: How much does an Audi A3 1.2 TFSI or 30 TFSI engine replacement cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: For an Audi A3 1.2 TFSI (CBZB/CBZA), expect £2,200-£3,500 supply-only for a rebuilt unit, or £600-£1,300 for a used engine. For the 30 TFSI (DLAA), rebuilt units typically range £3,200-£4,500, with used options from £1,000-£1,800. Fitting adds approximately £520-£650 labour at UK specialist rates.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of timing chain failure in an Audi A3 1.2 TFSI or 30 TFSI?

acceptedAnswer.text: The most common warning sign on EA111 and EA211 1.2 TFSI engines is a metallic rattling noise on cold start lasting 1-3 seconds. This is the tensioner losing hydraulic pressure. Other symptoms include engine management light illumination, timing-related fault codes, and eventually misfiring or non-start if the chain jumps. The 1.2 TFSI and 1.4 TFSI are the most susceptible to this issue.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in an Audi A3 1.2 TFSI or 30 TFSI?

acceptedAnswer.text: It depends on your A3's value. On 8P/8V examples worth under £4,000: a used engine at £600-£1,200 plus fitting often makes more sense than a rebuilt unit. On cars worth £5,000+: a rebuilt engine at £2,200-£3,500 is financially viable and carries a 12-month warranty. For 8Y 30 TFSI models worth £14,000+, a rebuilt engine at £3,200-£4,500 is a small percentage of the vehicle's value.

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between the Audi A3 1.2 TFSI CBZB and CBZA engines?

acceptedAnswer.text: Both are 1.2-litre TFSI engines, but they belong to different families. The CBZB (2010-2012, 8P) is an EA111 engine with 105hp, known for timing chain tensioner failure. The CBZA (2012-2016, 8V) is an EA211 engine with 105-110hp, featuring an improved design but still with timing chain concerns. The later CYZA (2014-2016) is similar to CBZA with minor calibration differences.

mainEntity.name: How long does an Audi A3 1.2 TFSI or 30 TFSI engine replacement take?

acceptedAnswer.text: A straight engine swap on an Audi A3 1.2 TFSI or 30 TFSI typically takes 8-10 hours labour at a specialist, including transfer of ancillary components. Most workshops complete the job in 1-2 working days.

mainEntity.name: Is the Audi A3 1.2 TFSI or 30 TFSI engine reliable?

acceptedAnswer.text: The EA111 1.2 TFSI (CBZB, 2010-2012) has a known timing chain tensioner weakness that makes it unreliable if not proactively maintained - tensioner failure can occur from 45,000 miles. The EA211 1.2 TFSI (CBZA/CYZA, 2012-2016) is improved but still has timing chain concerns. The 30 TFSI (DLAA, 2020+) is generally reliable, with occasional timing chain noise and mild-hybrid system complexity. Rebuilt units include upgraded components addressing original flaws.

historyTimeline.h2: Audi A3 1.2 TFSI & 30 TFSI - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The Audi A3 1.2 TFSI arrived with the second-generation A3 (8P) facelift in 2010 as Audi's entry-level petrol option, offering a surprisingly refined 105hp from just 1.2 litres. The 1.2 TFSI badge continued into the third-generation 8V (2012-2016), before being replaced by the 30 TFSI badge on the fourth-generation 8Y (2020+), which uses a 1.0-litre three-cylinder mild-hybrid engine producing 110hp.

milestones.description: Second-generation A3 (8P facelift) launches with 1.2 TFSI CBZB engine, 105hp (77kW), 1.2-litre four-cylinder turbocharged EA111
Third-generation A3 (8V) launched, 1.2 TFSI continues with 105-110hp output
End of 1.2 TFSI production in 8V; replaced by 1.0 TFSI in some markets
Fourth-generation A3 (8Y) launched with 30 TFSI badging - 1.0-litre three-cylinder DLAA engine, 110hp (81kW), mild-hybrid, EA211 Evo

commonProblems.h2: Audi A3 1.2 TFSI & 30 TFSI Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The Audi A3 1.2 TFSI and 30 TFSI present two distinct reliability profiles. Early EA111 1.2 TFSI units (CBZB, 2010-2012) are known for timing chain tensioner failure - a potentially catastrophic issue that can destroy the engine if ignored. Later EA211 1.2 TFSI units (CBZA, CYZA, 2012-2016) have improved but still suffer timing chain concerns. The latest 30 TFSI (DLAA, 2020+) uses a 1.0-litre three-cylinder EA211 Evo with mild-hybrid assistance and is generally more reliable. Rebuilt Audi A3 1.2 TFSI and 30 TFSI engines through EnginesMarket include upgraded timing components addressing these original failure points, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: Timing Chain Tensioner Failure - Why the Audi A3 1.2 TFSI EA111 Wears Prematurely
problems.rootCause: The EA111 1.2 TFSI uses a hydraulic timing chain tensioner that relies on oil pressure. When the engine is switched off, the tensioner can lose hydraulic pressure and fail to lock properly. This allows the chain to slacken, causing a metallic rattle on cold start. If ignored, the chain can jump timing or snap, leading to catastrophic engine damage. Some chains have been known to fail as early as 45,000 miles due to manufacturing defects.
